# Foundation Models & Multi-Scenario

Shared foundations, multi-task learning and transfer across scenarios.

| <a id="paper-2402-06859"></a>**LiRank: Industrial Large Scale Ranking Models at LinkedIn** | LinkedIn | KDD | 2024 | `Foundation Model` `Multi-task` `Quantization` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06859) | LiRank reports a production ranking framework combining residual cross networks, Transformers and dense gating. It also covers calibration, exploration–exploitation and model compression through quantization and vocabulary reduction. Its contribution is the practical integration of modeling and deployment choices across several ranking tasks, rather than a single isolated interaction operator. |
| <a id="paper-2508-02929"></a>**Realizing Scaling Laws in Recommender Systems: A Foundation-Expert Paradigm for Hyperscale Model Deployment** | Meta | arXiv | 2025 | `Foundation Model` `MoE` `Serving` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02929) | The Foundation-Expert paradigm transfers a large recommendation model's knowledge through target-aware embeddings rather than only teacher predictions. A central model represents a user's interest in a particular item given the full history, and lightweight surface-specific experts combine that representation with local features. This provides contextualized shared knowledge while leaving each surface room to specialize. |
| <a id="paper-2509-18091"></a>**OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking System** | Shopee | KDD | 2026 | `Foundation Model` `Architecture` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18091) | OnePiece enriches retrieval and ranking inputs with structured preference and scenario context, then refines representations through block-wise latent reasoning. Progressive multi-task training uses chains of user feedback to supervise the intermediate steps. The approach explores whether better context organization and repeated hidden-state refinement can improve a cascade beyond replacing its backbone alone. |
| <a id="paper-2502-08309"></a>**LUM: Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model** | Alibaba | WSDM | 2026 | `Foundation Model` `Scaling Law` `Knowledge Distillation` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309) | LUM addresses the gap between end-to-end generative recommendation and the feature, architecture and serving practices of industrial recommenders. It proposes a three-step large-user-model paradigm intended to preserve practical compatibility while benefiting from model scaling. The paper evaluates whether increased capacity translates into both stronger offline predictions and gains in a production A/B test. |
| <a id="paper-2602-11235"></a>**MTFM: A Scalable and Alignment-Free Foundation Model for Industrial Recommendation in Meituan** | Meituan | KDD | 2026 | `Foundation Model` `Training Efficiency` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11235) | MTFM learns across recommendation scenarios without first forcing their inputs into an identical schema. It represents cross-domain signals as heterogeneous tokens and aggregates examples by user, while grouped-query and hybrid target attention reduce cost. Kernel fusion and less CPU–GPU blocking complement the model so multi-scenario data and capacity can scale together. |
| <a id="paper-2606-00422"></a>**UniPinRec: Unifying Generative Retrieval and Ranking at Pinterest Scale** | Pinterest | RecSys (Industry) | 2026 | `Foundation Model` `Generative Rec` `Serving` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00422) | UniPinRec unifies retrieval and ranking beyond sharing a backbone: the stages also share input organization, training and serving computation. One history encoder feeds task-specific retrieval and ranking heads, with masked-action learning and blended examples supporting joint objectives. Cross-stage key-value caches reuse history processing that would otherwise be duplicated. |
| <a id="paper-2606-16838"></a>**OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation** | Shopee / RUC | KDD | 2026 | `Multi-task` `Architecture` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838) | OneRank brings task-specific learning inside the Transformer rather than attaching static task heads to a task-agnostic encoder. Private task channels select information and contextualize candidates, while controlled sharing and gradient detachment reduce interference between objectives. Dynamic matching replaces fixed feed-forward scoring, making predictions depend on each task's learned context. |
| <a id="paper-2606-19635"></a>**Token Factory: Efficiently Integrating Diverse Signals into Large Recommendation Models** | Google | RecSys (Industry) | 2026 | `Foundation Model` `Tokenization` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19635) | Token Factory converts heterogeneous recommendation signals into learned continuous tokens that a large recommendation model can consume directly. This avoids expanding every signal into text or long discrete sequences. Its role is an input interface and compression layer, allowing traditional features to enter Transformer-based recommenders without excessive prompt length and memory cost. |
| <a id="paper-2608-18606"></a>**OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking** | Xiaohongshu | arXiv | 2026 | `Multi-scenario` `Sequence Modeling` `Foundation Model` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606) | OneModel joins user behavior from organic recommendation, advertising and commerce streams into shared event sequences. A long-context backbone learns common user representations, while scenario-aware modulation preserves each stream's needs. Multi-objective training and shared user-side serving computation make this a platform-wide ranking framework rather than several disconnected models. |
| <a id="paper-2608-25546"></a>**AMBER: An Event is Worth One Token — Event Tokenization for Industrial-scale LLM Recommendation** | Meta | arXiv | 2026 | `Tokenization` `Foundation Model` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25546) | AMBER asks how much information each interaction token should contain, not just how many tokens a model can process. An end-to-end tokenizer compresses the event's user, item, context and outcome snapshot into one representation. Precomputing and caching these Event Tokens lets richer event detail improve modeling without requiring all encoding work during each serving request. |
| <a id="paper-2609-28589"></a>**OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender** | ByteDance | arXiv | 2026 | `Architecture` `MoE` `Foundation Model` `Serving` | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589) | OneTrans-V2 extends a shared Transformer across retrieval, pre-ranking and fine-ranking, encoding user history once while retaining stage-specific candidate processing. Joint training and internal distillation connect the stages, and sparse experts expand shared capacity. Decision-conditioned generation steers retrieval toward different objectives, while sequence-centered training and serving reuse expensive history computation. |
